item.title: Self-Hosted Linux Mandatory Access Control: SELinux vs AppArmor vs SMACK (2026)
item.description: Mandatory Access Control (MAC) is the most powerful security mechanism available on Linux. Unlike Discretionary Access Control (DAC), where file owners decide who gets access, MAC enforces system-wide security policies that even root cannot bypass. For self-hosted servers running critical infrastructure — web applications, databases, mail servers, and container workloads — implementing a MAC framework is essential defense-in-depth.
